newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities move upwards.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities move upwards.

text.p: Singapore government securities closed higher on Friday due to lower interest rates in the market, dealers said.
"The market has moved upwards mainly because of the low interest rates," said a local dealer.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at 2.82/2.77 percent compared to 2.88/2.83 percent on Thursday. One-year closed at 2.70/2.65 percent against the previous 2.73/2.68 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 moved up to S$98.54/98.59 compared with Thursday's S$98.50/98.60, September 2001 eased to S$96.20/96.25 from the previous S$96.45/96.55. June 2003 closed slightly higher at S$94.32/94.37 from S$94.23/94.33.
The overnight interbank offered rate moved up 3/8 percentage point to 3 2-7/8 percent versus Thursday's 2-5/8 2-1/2 percent.
